stem: A 4-year-old with fever has a seizure affecting one arm and one side of the face; which feature makes this concerning?

options.text: It occurs under 6 years of age

explanation: Focal seizure activity is concerning because febrile seizures are typically generalised rather than focal.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Neurology Seizures - Emergency Management

rationale: Focal semiology is a red flag in a febrile seizure and suggests the event is not a typical simple febrile seizure.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this is within the usual age range for febrile seizures and is not the concerning feature here.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because focal seizure activity is a red flag and atypical for a simple febrile seizure.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a post-ictal phase can occur after febrile seizures and does not by itself make the seizure focal.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because fever is part of the context of a febrile seizure and is not the feature that raises concern.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because childhood alone is too non-specific to indicate a red flag.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
